title: C-peptide

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: C-peptide is made by the pancreas at the same time as insulin and in equal amounts. Because it is not affected by insulin taken as medicine, a C-peptide test gives an accurate picture of how much insulin the body makes on its own.
context: Results are read together with a blood glucose test and depend on your age, health, and medicines. You may need to fast for 8 to 12 hours, or the test may be done after eating.
aboveRange: May mean the body is making a lot of insulin, as can happen with type 2 diabetes
May relate to Cushing's syndrome, a pancreatic tumor (insulinoma), a kidney condition, or a low blood potassium level
belowRange: May mean the body is not making enough insulin, as can happen with type 1 diabetes and sometimes type 2 diabetes
May relate to taking a lot of insulin as medicine, a serious infection, Addison disease, or a liver condition
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
